extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, journalism students and news organizations
extracted.subtask_description: A field-wide code of ethics that sets principles and specific practices for journalists and news organizations on gathering, reporting, and correcting news. Covers truth-seeking, harm minimization, independence, and accountability across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It — test accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core mandate to verify information from all sources; emphasizes avoiding inadvertent errors and prohibits deliberate distortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — seek responses from subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires active efforts to contact and allow subjects to respond to allegations before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — identify sources when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer named sources; provide context on reliability when using sources to help the audience evaluate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — protect and clarify promises of anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat promises of anonymity seriously: evaluate motives, explain conditions to the audience, and honor commitments to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — avoid misrepresentation in headlines and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All packaging and promotional elements must accurately reflect content and context; avoid sensationalism and misleading emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — do not distort photos or video
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits technical clarity enhancements but forbids altering content; require labeling for montages and illustrations to avoid deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — avoid misleading re-enactments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staged scenes must be rare and clearly labeled; do not present re-enactments as actual events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — undercover methods only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public. Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undercover tactics are a last resort — require public vital interest justification and on-air explanation of methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on presenting others' work as one's own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — tell diverse human stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages coverage that reflects broad human experiences and perspectives, including unpopular topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — examine and avoid imposing cultural values
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-awareness about cultural bias; avoid moralizing or projecting one's own cultural assumptions onto subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively guard against using or reinforcing stereotypes across a wide range of identity and social categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide space for a broad range of perspectives while maintaining journalistic standards for context and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include marginalized or less-heard perspectives; weigh them on their merits and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — distinguish advocacy and news
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label opinion, analysis, and commentary so audiences can tell them apart from factual news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — distinguish news from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid native advertising or sponsored content that is not clearly disclosed; maintain separation between editorial and commercial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — ensure openness of public business
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize transparency in government and public institutions; use and defend access to public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — show compassion and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat vulnerable subjects with extra care and consider emotional impact when reporting and publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — sensitivity with tragedy and grief
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid intrusive or sensational approaches to victims and grieving people; obtain consent and consider timing and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — recognize that reporting can cause harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest against possible harm; do not prioritize scoops over humane treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — respect privacy of private individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between public figures and private persons; intrusions into privacy require clear, overriding public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — show good taste; avoid lurid pandering
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject sensationalism and gratuitous detail that serves voyeuristic interests rather than newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — be cautious identifying juveniles and sex-crime victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise restraint in naming minors and sexual assault victims; follow legal and ethical norms for protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — be judicious before naming criminal suspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider accuracy, public interest, and potential harm to reputation when identifying alleged suspects prior to charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — balance fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care not to prejudice legal proceedings; provide context and avoid statements that could impair a defendant's right to fair trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from personal, financial, or other relationships that could compromise objectivity or create perceptions of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — remain free of compromising associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider off-duty activities, memberships, and relationships that could reflect on journalistic impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — refuse gifts and special treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline offers that could create dependence or obligations; avoid jobs or roles that present clear conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts cannot be avoided, be transparent with audiences about the nature of those conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — hold power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize watchdog reporting and investigative scrutiny of powerful institutions regardless of pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — deny favored treatment to advertisers and interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep editorial decisions independent of commercial or political influence; resist advertiser interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — avoid paying for information or bidding for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create perverse incentives by paying for information or engaging in competitive bidding that distorts reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — clarify coverage and invite dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively explain editorial choices and encourage public engagement and questions about reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — encourage public grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide channels for complaints and treat them seriously as part of accountability practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — admit mistakes and correct promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about errors; correct the record quickly and conspicuously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — expose unethical practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report on wrongdoing within the profession; uphold the same standards expected of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — abide by the same high standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistency between reporting standards applied to subjects and to the profession itself.
